title: phylotypr
text: get started ’ll need install phylotypr using either commands: get access packages function demonstration version training data, ’ll need run library() function.
code: # devtools::install_github("mothur/phylotypr") #install development version install.packages("phylotypr") # install stable version from CRAN library(phylotypr)

title: phylotypr
text: can classify sequence, need generate database. can done using build_kmer_database() function takes several seconds execute. phylotypr includes two databases: rdp_trainset9 rdp_trainset9_pds. want others, encouraged install {phylotyprrefdata} package GitHub. can also create reference set using create_database(). details, see “Alternative databases” section end vignette. ’ll use rdp_trainset9_pds tutorial. default, build_kmer_database() use 8-nt long kmers calculate probabilities. size can altered user needed, 8-nt performs well shouldn’t need adjusted.
code: db <- build_kmer_database(rdp_trainset9_pds)

title: phylotypr
text: classify sequence need DNA sequence character object like unknown . unknown object can classified using classify_sequences() along database object (.e., db). classification algorithm makes use random number generator, strongly encourage set seed get consistent results. needs set classify_sequences() set.seed(). default seed 1. output classify_sequences data frame taxonomic levels kingdom (domain) genus confidence scores sequence taxonomic levels example, ’ll notice family genus assignment confidence scores 80%. value commonly used mothur used RDP website. filter classification level confidence, can use filter_taxonomy() function: see “Porphyromonadaceae” “Barnesiella” names removed along confidence score. convert list format string, can use print_taxonomy() function:
code: unknown <- "TACGGAGGATGCGAGCGTTATCCGGATTTATTGGGTTTAAAGGGTGCGTAGGCGGATCGTTAAGTCAGTGGTCAAATTGAGGGGCTCAACCCCTTCCCGCCATTGAAACTGGCGATCTTGAGTGGAAGAGAAGTATGCGGAATGCGTGGTGTAGCGGTGAAATGCATAGATATCACGCAGAACCCCGATTGCGAAGGCAGCATGCCGGCTTCCTACTGACGCTCATGCACGAAAGTGTGGGTAACGAACAGG" consensus <- classify_sequences(sequence = unknown, database = db, seed = 123) consensus #>   sequence_name level      taxonomy confidence #> 1             1     1      Bacteria        100 #> 2             1     2 Bacteroidetes         98 #> 3             1     3   Bacteroidia         82 #> 4             1     4 Bacteroidales         82 filtered <- filter_taxonomy(consensus) filtered #>   sequence_name level      taxonomy confidence #> 1             1     1      Bacteria        100 #> 2             1     2 Bacteroidetes         98 #> 3             1     3   Bacteroidia         82 #> 4             1     4 Bacteroidales         82 print_taxonomy(filtered) #>   sequence_name #> 1             1 #>                                                            taxonomy #> 1 Bacteria(100);Bacteroidetes(98);Bacteroidia(82);Bacteroidales(82)

what: Classifying multiple unknown sequences in parallel
title: phylotypr
text: phylotypr package allows run classify_sequences() parallel. , computer 8 processors, classify_sequences() split data 8 chunks classify chunk separately pulling together. see many processors available, can run following: default, classify_sequences() use processors. need limit number processors, can use num_processors argument
code: parallelly::availableCores() #> system  #>      4 read_fasta(phylotypr_example("miseq_sop.fasta.gz")) |>   classify_sequences(database = db, seed = 123, num_processors = 2) |>   print_taxonomy() |>   head() #>                                 sequence_name #> 1 M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_10331_23332 #> 2 M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_10382_22128 #> 3 M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_10491_15766 #> 4  M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_10877_9025 #> 5 M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_11035_15765 #> 6  M00967_43_000000000A3JHG_1_1101_11296_4480 #>                                                                                                                        taxonomy #> 1            Bacteria(100);Firmicutes(98);Clostridia(98);Clostridiales(98);Lachnospiraceae(88);Lachnospiraceae_unclassified(88) #> 2         Bacteria(100);Firmicutes(100);Clostridia(100);Clostridiales(100);Ruminococcaceae(99);Ruminococcaceae_unclassified(99) #> 3 Bacteria(100);Bacteroidetes(100);Bacteroidia(99);Bacteroidales(99);Porphyromonadaceae(96);Porphyromonadaceae_unclassified(96) #> 4         Bacteria(100);Proteobacteria(100);Gammaproteobacteria(100);Pseudomonadales(100);Moraxellaceae(100);Acinetobacter(100) #> 5         Bacteria(100);Firmicutes(100);Clostridia(100);Clostridiales(100);Lachnospiraceae(97);Lachnospiraceae_unclassified(97) #> 6            Bacteria(100);Firmicutes(95);Clostridia(94);Clostridiales(93);Ruminococcaceae(88);Ruminococcaceae_unclassified(88)

title: phylotypr
text: Consider results classifying unknown three times three different seeds: ’ll notice classification three replicates varies slightly. , due use random number generator getting confidence scores bounce around 80%, results different levels filtering. get stable classification, setting random number generator seed consistent value seed. get precise confidence score, set num_bootstraps = 1000 classify_sequences(). forewarned function take 10-times longer run 10-times number bootstraps!
code: classify_sequences(sequence = unknown, database = db, seed = 1) |>   print_taxonomy() #>   sequence_name #> 1             1 #>                                                                                   taxonomy #> 1 Bacteria(100);Bacteroidetes(96);Bacteroidia(85);Bacteroidales(85);Porphyromonadaceae(84) classify_sequences(sequence = unknown, database = db, seed = 2) |>   print_taxonomy() #>   sequence_name #> 1             1 #>                                                                                   taxonomy #> 1 Bacteria(100);Bacteroidetes(95);Bacteroidia(83);Bacteroidales(83);Porphyromonadaceae(82) classify_sequences(sequence = unknown, database = db, seed = 3) |>   print_taxonomy() #>   sequence_name #> 1             1 #>                                                            taxonomy #> 1 Bacteria(100);Bacteroidetes(92);Bacteroidia(80);Bacteroidales(80) classify_sequences(sequence = unknown, database = db, num_bootstraps = 1000,                    seed = 123) |>   print_taxonomy() #>   sequence_name #> 1             1 #>                                                                   taxonomy #> 1 Bacteria(99.9);Bacteroidetes(96.5);Bacteroidia(83.9);Bacteroidales(83.9)

title: Classify a vector of 16S rRNA gene sequence fragments — classify_sequences
code: kmer_size <- 3 reference_names <- c("seq_1", "seq_2", "seq_3") reference_sequences <- c("ATGCGCTA", "ATGCGCTC", "ATGCGCTC") reference_genera <- c("A", "B", "B") reference <- create_database(reference_names, reference_sequences, reference_genera)  db <- build_kmer_database(reference, kmer_size)  unknown_sequence <- c("ATGCGCTC", "ATGCGCTC", "ATGCGCTC") unknown_id <- c("seq_1", "seq_2", "seq_3")  classify_sequences(   sequence = unknown_sequence,   database = db,   kmer_size = kmer_size,   seed = 1,   num_processors = 1 ) #>   sequence_name level taxonomy confidence #> 1             1     1        B        100 #> 2             2     1        B        100 #> 3             3     1        B        100  classify_sequences(   sequence = unknown_sequence,   sequence_name = unknown_id,   database = db,   kmer_size = kmer_size ) #>   sequence_name level taxonomy confidence #> 1         seq_1     1        B        100 #> 2         seq_2     1        B        100 #> 3         seq_3     1        B        100  classify_sequences(   sequence = "ATGATCGAGTC",   database = db,   kmer_size = kmer_size,   min_confidence = 95 ) #>   sequence_name level taxonomy confidence #> 1             1     1        A         99  sequence_df <- data.frame(   seq_names = unknown_id,   seqs = unknown_sequence )  classify_sequences(sequence_df,   sequence_name = seq_names, sequence = seqs,   database = db, kmer_size = 3 ) #>   sequence_name level taxonomy confidence #> 1         seq_1     1        B        100 #> 2         seq_2     1        B        100 #> 3         seq_3     1        B        100
